_comment: Template for ~/.locus/data/dispatcher/<slug>/config.json. `dispatcher.py init` copies this, fills every label id from the workspace you name, and writes it. Nothing here is read at runtime from the plugin directory — the instance copy is the live one. A re-run of `init` against an existing instance fills in any `linear.labels`, `linear.modes` or `traits` key it has never heard of and creates the missing labels, so adding a mode here is how an installed instance learns about one.
_comment_decide: `decide` has its own trigger label but shares `investigating` as its working label, so eleven labels cover five modes. A working label is never read by any code — `linear_triggers` reads only `trigger` — so the only cost is that the board shows a decide worker and an investigate worker alike while they run, and the only benefit of a tenth label would be telling those two apart mid-flight. `blocked` is not in `modes` at all: it is a resting state a coordinator writes, never a trigger anything polls for.
_comment_review_desk: Review Desk, if it is installed: https://github.com/devergehq/review-desk. `mode` auto uses it when it is found and is otherwise silent; `on` is the same but fails `doctor` and tells the principal when it is not; `off` never calls it. Everything here is defaulted in code, so an instance whose config has no `review_desk` block behaves exactly as `auto` and needs no edit. `url` is only for the links a session puts in its messages and for `doctor`'s reachability line — nothing is driven over HTTP. `brief_gate` never writes the brief as needing no confirmation, with that reason; always writes it as needing the developer's and waits.
